scope: Owned localhost HTML article in a real Chrome tab with the released unpacked extension and native side panel. The fixture contains two inline SVG figures, each with a distinct caption and adjacent HTML label. Fast Capture and Scroll & capture must preserve each loaded graphic's decoded SVG geometry and interleave it with its own caption and label in rendered Article order. Before Deep capture the owned page changes a caption and bar geometry, so the visible result must prove a new capture generation.

runtime_attempt_001.result: The owned native browser reached Fast capture but the Article readiness wait timed out after 30 seconds; no mode was accepted.
runtime_attempt_001.diagnosis_limit: The first runner recorded no Article or Scrape pane sample. Source inspection shows rendered images use lazy loading, but the run does not establish whether image loading, capture, a visible error, or panel selection caused the timeout.
runtime_attempt_001.instrumentation_for_rerun: Each Article wait sample preserves bounded pane state, error-card text, image load and viewport flags, decoded SVG path/bar coordinates, and the positions of expected text and image markers. On failure, the runner captures its owned panel to a stable test-results path before harness cleanup. Assertion and settled-state stages remain distinct, with the assertion label retained in the failure detail. No extension behavior or acceptance expectation was changed.

runtime_attempt_002.result: Fast capture completed and the Article pane contained both SVG data payloads, both captions and labels, and the expected text/graphic order. The second SVG stayed unloaded below the viewport with loading=lazy, so the runner's image-load wait timed out before accepting Fast or attempting Deep.
runtime_attempt_002.diagnosis: The acceptance runner waited for a lazy image that it never scrolled into view. This is a runner interaction gap; native scrolling and the loaded-image assertion are now explicit. Product extraction remains unverified until the guarded rerun.
